claim: Consequential payroll requests already in flight are cancelled when live payroll authority is revoked.

scope.environment: local synthetic authenticated HTTP and SQLite
scope.scale: one payroll actor, one administrator, one held request

causalOrdering: Payroll request headers and half of the JSON body were sent.
The session last_seen transition proved actor(req) had completed against the pre-revocation user row.
An authenticated company administrator removed all permissions from that payroll account.
The held request body was completed only after the revocation returned HTTP 200.
The held request returned HTTP 200 and persisted one new payroll adjustment.
rootCause: server.cjs snapshots actor permissions before awaiting the request body. The mutation and payroll dispatcher later authorize against that stale actor object and do not re-read live authority immediately before the consequential state transition.
repairAcceptance: Re-read and validate live user/session authority inside the same protected mutation boundary immediately before a consequential state change.
Reject a request when its permissions, account status or session validity changed after initial authentication.
Prove no state, audit, lineage or export mutation occurs for the rejected request.
Repeat under concurrent requests and after restart, then reproduce in the exact Node 22 packaged and hosted candidate.
